The workGet in touch

Fiber quality / Measurement / People

Pieces of an ongoing
system-level project.

These are some of the things I’ve been thinking about and working on: how we build fiber, how we decide it’s good, and what happens after we leave.

There’s plenty here still to test, refine, and correct. I’m sharing the work as it develops. If something catches your interest—or you see it differently—I’d like to hear about it.

Open questions. Working ideas. Room to change my mind.

Three places to start

Two short pieces and something you can try.

01 / MEASUREMENT
Working idea

Can we trust the measurement?

As AI takes on more quality decisions, the physical test still has to mean something. I’m exploring what better equipment stewardship could do for today’s work, tomorrow’s datasets, and technician readiness.

Read the measurement integrity piece ↗
02 / LONG-TERM QUALITY
Question I’m investigating

What does a passing strand tell us about tomorrow?

I want to connect what we see at installation with what happens later. Which details might help us recognize a path that passes today but is more likely to need attention down the road?

Read the predictive quality piece ↗
03 / LEARNING IN PRACTICE
Interactive prototype

Fiber Field Lab

A place to try some of the thinking. Short lessons and synthetic OTDR scenarios explore what we observe, how we interpret it, and what we should verify before acting.

Try the training lab ↗
OBSERVE → INTERPRET → VERIFY → ACTILLUSTRATION

Why these belong
in the same conversation.

The equipment affects the evidence. The evidence shapes decisions. Training, workflow, and incentives influence what people do with it. I’m interested in how those pieces interact—and where a practical change might improve the whole system.

Trust the measurement→Learn from outcomes→Improve the work

What do you think?

I’d rather start a conversation than have the last word.
